evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: In AXIS, 723 patients with previously treated advanced renal cell carcinoma received axitinib or sorafenib. The current EMA table reports median progression-free survival of 6.8 versus 4.7 months (hazard ratio 0.67; 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.81). Overall survival was not significantly different. Results varied with previous therapy; this does not compare axitinib with every current combination.

evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after prior VEGF-targeted therapy
evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: METEOR compared cabozantinib with everolimus after VEGF-targeted therapy. The primary progression-free analysis in 375 patients showed medians of 7.4 versus 3.8 months (hazard ratio 0.58; 95% confidence interval 0.45–0.74). In the full 658-patient population, a subsequent overall-survival analysis showed 21.4 versus 16.5 months (hazard ratio 0.66; 95% confidence interval 0.53–0.83). These are group estimates from different analyses, not an individual prediction.
limitations: Historical comparators may differ from current treatment options.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Temsirolimus inhibits a protein called mTOR, part of the signalling system that controls cell growth, protein production and blood-vessel development. This can slow tumour growth. mTOR also supports normal immune and metabolic functions, explaining infection risk and changes in glucose or cholesterol.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The usual dose is 25 mg by intravenous infusion over 30 minutes once a week. The NCCP calendar lists Days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of each 28-day cycle. Continue while helpful and tolerable; there is no routine week off.

NCCP specifies diphenhydramine 25–50 mg IV, or a similar antihistamine, about 30 minutes before each dose. Your unit confirms its prescribed equivalent.

Use gentle mouth care and report ulcers early. Review infection prevention, diabetes and lipid management. Preventive medicine against Pneumocystis pneumonia may be considered if you also take corticosteroids or other immune-suppressing medicines; it is not automatically required for everyone.

The current EMA table distinguishes the prespecified interim hazard ratio of 0.73 (95% confidence interval 0.58–0.92) from the final analysis of 0.78 (0.63–0.97). This historical comparison does not establish superiority over modern first-line combinations.
limitations: Historical comparators may differ from current treatment options.
Do not transfer results between different drugs, combinations or disease settings.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: These materials cover olaparib after treatment for high-risk early breast cancer. Other cancers use different eligibility, duration and follow-up; use the matching NCCP indication and your treating team’s plan. Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Olaparib (Lynparza): BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course.
key_points: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.
Usually 300 mg twice daily; follow the individual prescription

For breast indication 00588h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.

This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated.

Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.
There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.
Keep 00588h patient material separate from shared ovarian/prostate/pancreatic durations and consent.

Breast high-risk TNBC after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: residual invasive disease; after adjuvant chemotherapy: node-positive or node-negative tumour≥2 cm. HR-positive/HER2-negative after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: residual disease plus CPS+EG≥3; after adjuvant chemotherapy:≥4 positive nodes.
NCCP ideally starts within 12 weeks after the last surgery/chemotherapy/radiation; this is an ideal target, not a hard exclusion. OlympiA required local therapy at least 2 weeks before enrolment.
Initial blood recovery to CTCAE grade≤1 differs from NCCP continuation ANC≥1/platelets≥100 thresholds.
NCCP/SmPC differ at exact CrCl30, severe renal/dialysis and Child-PughC. Those outputs require source reconciliation without an automatic dose.
Avoid importing an ovarian clinical-trial CT schedule into disease-free adjuvant breast follow-up. No universal olaparib echo/ECG/DXA schedule.
Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor; this matters when designing the oral antiemetic script.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.
eligibility_orientation: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.
important_cautions: This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated.

Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss effective contraception before treatment; EMA recommends two reliable complementary methods for women during treatment and for six months afterwards. Men and their partners need contraception during treatment and for three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for one month after the last dose.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high emetic risk. Agree an anti-sickness plan under local policy, and seek review if oral intake falls. The SmPC describes early/intermittent symptoms; do not automatically copy an intravenous chemotherapy antiemetic cycle.

Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor in NCCP 00588 and can increase olaparib exposure. The prescriber/pharmacist should choose and reconcile supportive medicines; never add an antiemetic from another regimen without checking.
Anaemia or other low counts can lead to interruption, dose adjustment, transfusion or additional investigation. There is no universal routine G-CSF course for every person on this regimen.

Review all prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs and herbal products. Strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers can change exposure. Avoid grapefruit products and seek advice before starting anything new.
NCCP allows consideration of a proton pump inhibitor under local policy. This is symptom- and patient-dependent, rather than a compulsory medication for everyone.
patient_education: Contact the oncology team urgently for fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, new or worsening breathlessness/cough, severe weakness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse require emergency help.

Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double it. Check tablet strength after any dose change.
special_support: There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.

baseline: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start.
before_each_cycle: NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change.
ongoing: Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.
There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.

After early breast cancer treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation, or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. Routine mammography of the mastectomy side is not required. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended solely to look for recurrence in an asymptomatic person. Safety blood tests for ongoing olaparib are a separate requirement. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.
No routine tumour markers for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance.
priority_toxicities: Nausea, vomiting, reduced appetite and indigestion
Fatigue and anaemia
Low neutrophils or platelets, with infection or bleeding risk
Diarrhoea or altered taste
Uncommon but serious pneumonitis or drug-induced liver injury
Rare serious marrow disorders, including MDS/AML
Venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; risk differs by treatment setting
Fetal harm; contraception and breastfeeding restrictions
urgent_review_signals: Contact the oncology team urgently for fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, new or worsening breathlessness/cough, severe weakness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse require emergency help.

practical_workflow: Olaparib follows the chemotherapy and local-treatment plan. The oncology team decides when and at what dose to restart after blood recovery or symptom improvement. Do not calculate a catch-up dose or restart automatically because a calendar month has passed.

Agree the stop date and ongoing breast follow-up. Endocrine treatment and breast surveillance may continue. Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections, bruising or breathlessness even after olaparib finishes.
observation_and_access: No home infusion pump is part of this regimen. Access for an infusion is agreed with the team.

context_profiles.regimen_role: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after a new hormonal agent
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Help control prostate cancer that has progressed despite hormone treatment, where a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation is confirmed.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after a new hormonal agent
context_profiles.component_rationale: Olaparib blocks poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), which helps repair damaged DNA. A cancer cell with a pathogenic BRCA1/2 change already has difficulty using another repair pathway. Blocking PARP can leave too much damage for the cell to survive. This is why a validated mutation result matters.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food, continuously while helpful and tolerable. Kidney function, interactions or side effects can change the prescribed dose. This prostate course does not use the one-year breast or two-year ovarian limit.
key_points: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food, continuously while helpful and tolerable. Kidney function, interactions or side effects can change the prescribed dose. This prostate course does not use the one-year breast or two-year ovarian limit.

Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Persistent low counts after an interruption may need specialist blood investigations. Review new cough, breathlessness, bleeding and leg swelling promptly.
Confirm the pathogenic germline or tumour BRCA1/2 result and previous treatment. Continue prescribed androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) unless you have had surgical castration.

NCCP classes oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk. The team considers anti-sickness medicine and a proton pump inhibitor for stomach protection under local policy. Obtain a written prevention/rescue plan and report persistent nausea or inability to take tablets.

treatment_rationale.summary: Olaparib blocks poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), which helps repair damaged DNA. A cancer cell with a pathogenic BRCA1/2 change already has difficulty using another repair pathway. Blocking PARP can leave too much damage for the cell to survive. This is why a validated mutation result matters. Continue ADT, which keeps testosterone low, unless you have had surgical castration. Olaparib targets DNA repair rather than replacing hormone suppression. Abiraterone and other androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) act on hormone signalling; adding or switching them needs a separate evidence-based plan. Radiotherapy can treat selected sites or relieve symptoms, with timing agreed by the team.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Help control prostate cancer that has progressed despite hormone treatment, where a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation is confirmed.
disease_and_biomarker_context: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after a new hormonal agent
eligibility_orientation: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after a new hormonal agent
Verify source performance status and organ-function requirements.
exclusion_orientation: Source contraindications, pregnancy where relevant, significant toxicity or interaction requiring review
important_cautions: NCCP 00588g: pathogenic germline or somatic BRCA1/2, mCRPC and progression after a new hormonal agent. A VUS is not equivalent.
Continue medical castration unless surgically castrated; no breast/ovarian time cap applies.
Preserve existing source-specific cytopenia, renal-boundary, liver, interaction and persistent marrow-toxicity rules; do not stack dose reductions.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: Confirm the pathogenic germline or tumour BRCA1/2 result and previous treatment. Continue prescribed androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) unless you have had surgical castration.

NCCP classes oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk. The team considers anti-sickness medicine and a proton pump inhibitor for stomach protection under local policy. Obtain a written prevention/rescue plan and report persistent nausea or inability to take tablets.
counselling: Swallow tablets whole; do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. Tablets and capsules are not interchangeable. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; never double up. Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges, and check all medicines with pharmacy.

Use a condom during treatment and for three months afterwards when having sex with a partner who is or could become pregnant. The partner should use highly effective contraception during that time. Do not donate sperm during treatment or for three months afterwards; discuss fertility preservation.

baseline: Validated BRCA1/2 result, full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Confirm recovery from previous blood toxicity and review current medicines, previous hormone treatment and ongoing testosterone suppression.
before_each_cycle: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Persistent low counts after an interruption may need specialist blood investigations. Review new cough, breathlessness, bleeding and leg swelling promptly.

priority_toxicities: Anaemia, sometimes requiring transfusion; low white cells and platelets with infection or bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, reduced appetite and taste changes
Fatigue, weakness, headache, dizziness and mouth soreness
Serious or persistent blood-count changes; rare myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia, sometimes fatal
New cough or breathlessness from pneumonitis, which can be serious or fatal
Blood clots in veins or lungs; seek urgent help for a swollen leg, chest pain or breathlessness
Liver injury and changes in kidney blood tests; organ function and interactions may require dose changes
Allergic reactions, possible fertility effects and harm to an unborn child

administration.cycle_and_sequence: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food, continuously while helpful and tolerable. Kidney function, interactions or side effects can change the prescribed dose. This prostate course does not use the one-year breast or two-year ovarian limit.

evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after a new hormonal agent
evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: In the BRCA1/2-mutated subgroup of PROfound, 160 patients received olaparib or the investigator’s choice of abiraterone or enzalutamide after progression on a new hormonal agent. Median radiological progression-free survival was 9.8 versus 3.0 months (hazard ratio 0.22; 95% confidence interval 0.15–0.32); median overall survival was 20.1 versus 14.4 months (hazard ratio 0.63; 0.42–0.95). These subgroup analyses were not controlled for multiple comparisons. They do not compare every modern alternative or establish the separate olaparib-plus-abiraterone regimen.
